L48: Section 2. In elections, the person receiving the highest number of votes for an office shall be deemed and declared to be elected to such office; and if two or more are to be elected to the same office, the several persons, to the number to be chosen to such office, receiving the highest number of votes, shall be deemed and declared to be elected; but persons receiving the same number of votes shall not be deemed to be elected if thereby a greater number would be elected than are to be chosen.
L49: Except as otherwise provided, this section shall apply to all nominations and elections by ballot at primaries or caucuses. Nothing herein shall derogate from the provisions of chapter fifty-four A.

L110:     * cite52†Sitemap L111: # Election Data & Statistics Hub
L112: 
L113: This page contains current and archived data and statistical information relating to the last several statewide elections. The information is categorized below by subject.
L114: ## Voter Registration
L115: 
L116: Voter registration and party enrollment statistics are published after the deadline for registration for each statewide election. In odd-numbered years, when there is no statewide election, statistics are published as of February 1.
L117: 
L118: Select an election below to download a .xlxs file containing detailed registration statistics by county, municipality, precinct, and party.

L177:   * cite73†November 2012 State Election L178: ## Voter Turnout Statistics
L179: 
L180: Our office maintains statistics relating to voter turnout in statewide elections. Below, you may find voter turnout information at the statewide level, dating back to 1948.
L181: 
L182: Local elections are administered by local election officials, and turnout information is not reported to the Elections Division. For information about voter turnout in local elections, contact the relevant local election office.
L183: ### Statewide Voter Turnout
L184: 
L185: cite74†Statewide Election Voter turnout, 1948-present L186: ### Detailed Voter Turnout
L187: 
L188: Detailed statistical information on voter turnout by municipality and method of voting is available for elections dating back to 2016. Below, you will find .xlxs files containing this data.
L189: 
L190: The below data includes information on the number and percentage of ballots cast by mail, early, and on Election Day. Information on rejected absentee and early ballots is also included. For primaries, a breakdown of turnout by party is provided.
L191: Notes: Large-scale voting by mail began with the 2020 State Primary. For prior elections, data is separated by absentee and/or early ballot. For elections since September 2020, data is categorized by the method through which the ballot was provided to the voter. Prior to 2020, early voting was not available for primaries.

L220:   * cite85†2016 State Election Turnout Statistics L221: ## Statewide Ballot Measure Statistics
L222: 
L223: Our office maintains statistical information on statewide ballot measures, dating back to 1919, the year that voters could first petition to place questions on the ballot.
L224: Statewide ballot measure statistics include information on the different types of ballot measures and how frequently they have appeared on ballots since 1919. For each question in each election, you will find the name of the question, the question type, the outcome of the vote, and the vote totals.
